expectations.text: Recommends SHA-256 (fast hash) over bcrypt for the stored key hashes
expectations.evidence: "use SHA-256, not bcrypt, for these keys."

expectations.text: Grounds the choice in entropy: slow hashes exist to defend low-entropy human passwords, and brute force is infeasible against a high-entropy generated key at any per-hash cost
expectations.evidence: "Passwords are low-entropy and human-chosen... A 40-character random key has about 160 bits... slow hash adds cost without adding security."

expectations.text: Cites bcrypt's 72-byte input truncation as a mechanical strike against bcrypt for long keys
expectations.evidence: "A 72-byte input limit. bcrypt silently truncates input at 72 bytes."

expectations.text: Points out that salted slow hashes cannot be looked up by hash equality, breaking the proposed loop-and-compare design
expectations.evidence: "Salted bcrypt hashes cannot be matched with WHERE hash = ?. That is why the loop exists"

expectations.text: Adds a short indexed plaintext key_prefix column for O(1) candidate lookup
expectations.evidence: key_prefix column and idx_api_keys_prefix; "plaintext lookup handle"

expectations.text: Requires constant-time comparison on the final hash check, naming the timing leak of a naive equality comparison
expectations.evidence: "Do not use ==, which leaks timing."
